minutes.headline: Selectmen approved sale of school construction bonds and accepted the Whitetail Crossing road layout.
minutes.summary: The board approved the sale of general obligation bonds for the middle high school project after a financial advisor explained rates, remaining borrowing and tax impact. It accepted the road layout of Whitetail Crossing for town meeting, and held a long first discussion of a draft earth removal bylaw, including moving the permit to a land use board. Committee reports covered the school committee's FY16 budget request, the audit and Chapter 90 funds.

public_comment.topic: Announcement of the Lions Club pancake breakfast and the Boys and Girls Club game show fundraiser, with a request that the board field a team.
Chair asked for public comment; none offered.

budget_items.what_was_said: Board asked to approve the sale of general obligation bonds for local share of the middle high school project.
The town sold an earlier bond issue a few months earlier to cover temporary financing.
Six bids were received and the town kept its bond rating.
About another amount is expected to be borrowed in a year, assuming the project is on budget and MSBA pays the maximum grant.
The net impact on the tax rate is estimated slightly lower than previously projected, assuming higher interest on the later issue.
A member said they expected to leave less for next year; the advisor said the figure is a likely worst case and overborrowing creates problems.
The motion states the bond price paid by the winning bidder.
Premium above cost of issuance would be voted by town meeting toward the project.
Board discussed when to require a performance bond for earth removal permits and cash bond options.
Accounts payable, payroll and payroll deduction warrants read.
A member reported the superintendent's FY16 school budget request was above the committee target.
An abatement request received a low priority rating from capital planning.
The governor released remaining Chapter 90 funds, worth roughly a stated amount to the town for road work.

decisions.decision: Members to send comments on the draft earth removal bylaw to the land use director within a week; revised draft returns the first meeting in February, then a workshop with the planning board, then distribution to permit holders.
Board and committee appreciation social set for January 27, 6 to 7:30, location to be confirmed.
Board agreed a bylaw review committee is needed.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved the sale of general obligation bonds for the town's local share of the middle high school project.
The board accepted the Whitetail Crossing road layout, as reviewed by the planning board, with the noted contingencies.
The board held a long first discussion of a draft earth removal bylaw, including moving the permit to a land use board and when to require performance bonds.
Members were asked to send comments on the draft bylaw to the land use director within a week; a revised draft returns the first meeting in February.
A member reported the superintendent's FY16 school budget request was above the school committee's target.

why_it_matters: The bond sale sets the borrowing cost for the town's share of the school project, which is repaid through the tax rate; the advisor's estimate was slightly lower than projected, with more borrowing possible in a year.
The earth removal bylaw would change who issues gravel permits and what bonds permit holders must post, and it is likely to come to residents as a town meeting article.
The FY16 school request above the committee target is a budget gap that will need resolving before town meeting.
watch_next: Revised earth removal bylaw draft at the first Select Board meeting in February, then a workshop with the planning board.
Town meeting votes on the Whitetail Crossing road layout and on applying the bond premium to the school project.
